mappings.note: Onset of the reproductive phase in women is a human-reproduction process to be explained, which is exactly C-SCI2.2-LO-2. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because nothing here is applied to daily living - it asks what happens in the body.

Choosing the right meal for an adolescent is applying science to day-to-day life, the adolescence strand of C-SCI3.2-LO-1. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, because no bodily process is being explained, a food choice is being made.
Sex determination by the XX chromosome combination is part of explaining reproduction in humans. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, whose reproduction example is the sexual/asexual split, not chromosomes.

Same mechanism as the previous item with the XY combination; explaining human reproduction is the only outcome that covers sex determination. The frame offers no finer distinction between the two cases.

The human chromosome count is the substrate for the sex-determination explanation and sits with reproduction in humans. Not C-SCI2.3-LO-3, which is about preparing and describing slides, not recalling a number.
Identifying an iron-rich food is a dietary choice made in daily life, so C-SCI3.2-LO-1. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because no cause-and-effect process is asked for, only what to eat.

Which gland makes adrenaline is part of explaining how the human body's endocrine control works. The frame has no separate endocrine outcome, so the human-process outcome C-SCI2.2-LO-2 is the only honest home.
A Y-bearing sperm determining the zygote's sex is the fertilisation mechanism, squarely reproduction in humans. Not the CG-level code, because a specific learning outcome fits.

That hormones control the changes of adolescence is the causal explanation of a human body process. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because nothing is being applied or acted on, the controlling agent is being named.
Recognising a balanced diet is an everyday application of nutrition science. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, which is about explaining processes inside the body rather than planning a meal.

The legal age of marriage belongs to the social/health side of adolescence that C-SCI3.2-LO-1 names, including challenging myths and taboos. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, because it is not a biological process at all.

Attributing AIDS to a virus relates a phenomenon to its cause, the pattern of C-SCI2.2-LO-1. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the pupil is not sorting microorganisms into useful and harmful, only naming the agent behind one disease.
Hormone transport by the bloodstream is a body process to be explained. Not C-SCI2.3-LO-4, which would require a labelled diagram or flow chart rather than recall of the route.
Where hormones are produced is part of the endocrine explanation covered by C-SCI2.2-LO-2. The frame offers one outcome for human body processes, so this recall cluster shares it.
The pituitary as the master gland is a fact about how endocrine control is organised, a human body process. No classification outcome applies: glands are not one of the pairs C-SCI1.1-LO-1 lists.

Pancreas-to-insulin is gland-to-secretion recall inside the endocrine explanation. Shares C-SCI2.2-LO-2 with the rest of this factual-recall cluster because the frame provides no more specific outcome.

Insulin regulating blood sugar is a physiological regulation mechanism, so the explain-processes outcome. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, whose causal examples are environmental (smog, acid rain), not homeostatic.

Linking goitre to an iodine deficiency relates a condition to its cause, which is C-SCI2.2-LO-1 rather than the explain-the-process sibling. Deliberately different from the neighbouring gland-recall items, which describe a working process rather than a cause.
That endocrine glands secrete hormones is the defining statement of the endocrine process. Kept at the LO rather than the C-SCI2.2 competency because the LO explicitly covers processes in humans.
Naming a pituitary hormone continues the endocrine explanation strand. No sibling fits: the classification outcomes list materials and organisms, not secretions.
Iodine as the element needed to build thyroxine is part of how the thyroid works. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because the question asks what the hormone is made of, not what goes wrong without it.
Thyroid-to-thyroxine is another gland-to-secretion fact within the endocrine process. Shares the outcome with its neighbours because the frame genuinely offers only one for human physiology.
Adrenaline acting in fear and excitement is the emergency response mechanism, a process to explain. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, since no day-to-day decision follows from it.
Menarche as the first menstruation is a reproductive event in humans. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which would apply to hygiene or myth-busting advice built on it, not the definition.

Menopause as the end of the reproductive phase is the mirror of the menarche item and belongs to reproduction in humans. The pair differs from each other in content but the frame has one outcome for both.
Defining puberty by the onset of reproductive maturity is a human reproduction process. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because no myth, taboo or daily practice is engaged.

Asking why adolescents must watch their diet turns nutrition into a daily-life decision about one's own body. Chosen over C-SCI2.2-LO-2 because the point of the item is the practical consequence, not the physiology.

Naming ploughing/tilling as loosening the soil is part of the crop-production practice C-SCI3.2-LO-1 names explicitly. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, which is about fertiliser, pesticide and resource restraint, not tillage.

Identifying a pesticide anchors on the only place pesticides appear in the frame, the judicious-use outcome C-SCI4.1-LO-1. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which covers the farming operations themselves rather than agrochemicals.

The seed drill being used for sowing is an implement-to-practice fact about increasing crop production. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, which requires the pupil to build a model and explain it, not recall a tool's use.

Knowing when rabi crops are harvested is the kharif/rabi classification named verbatim in C-SCI1.2-LO-1. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because it sorts crops by season rather than carrying out a farming practice.
Placing maize in the rainy (kharif) season is the same seasonal classification, applied to a named crop. Kept distinct from the practice items because the skill tested is sorting, not doing.
The implement used for weeding is a crop-production practice under C-SCI3.2-LO-1. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1: mechanical weeding is the alternative to weedicides, so no agrochemical restraint is at issue.
Transplantation of seedlings (paddy) is a sowing practice that raises yield. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, since no crop is being classified, a method is being identified.

Compost as natural manure is the organic alternative to chemical fertiliser, which is where the frame puts fertiliser judgement. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because the item is about the nature of the input, not the field operation.

BHC being an insecticide/pesticide again anchors on the controlled-use-of-pesticides outcome. Differs from the compost item in substance though it shares the code, the frame having a single agrochemical outcome.

Defining fertilisers as nutrient-rich chemical substances is the counterpart of the compost item and belongs to the same fertiliser outcome. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, whose classification examples do not include soil inputs.
Threshing, the separation of grain from chaff, is a post-harvest production practice. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, because no investigation is being conducted, a named operation is being recalled.

Humus as decayed organic matter is the natural route to soil fertility that sits beside manure in the judicious-use outcome. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because it describes the soil's own resource rather than a farming operation.
